title: Rulebook Decisions
description: Every call that shapes the new writing rulebook, in the order they depend on each other: requirements, your calls, proposed cuts, open clashes, settled items.
intro: These decide what goes into the new rulebook. They run in the order they depend on each other: the requirements first, then your calls from the business changes, then the rules I would cut or change, then the clashes still open, then everything already settled.
Pick one option per card. Notes are optional. Numbers run through the whole page, so any line can be named by its number. Picks save as you go, and I read them from here.

sections.title: The requirements
sections.sub: Every rule below was tested against these. Number 5 carries your note from today.

cards.title: What the writing rules are for
items: The book is the main job: finish 5 Laws of Lasting Change from what already exists (the brain, the articles, your notes), at Clear and Dweck standard.
Articles and letters are written to book standard and feed the chapters.
Case studies read like Dweck, sound like you, and stay inside the built-detail lines.
The reader keeps trying but never finishes. Many read English as a second language. Parents matter. Introverts are one track, not the main idea.

Everything is true and from your material, and clients stay hidden. Being open and vulnerable is welcome, often good. What is out is a line that reads against you out of context. Everyone is resourceful.
Your workflow: the brain is the one home of material, you mark up in Google Docs, key moments come before the chapter, one chat per piece.
The writer follows the crucial rules every time, on far fewer rule tokens.
options: Needs a change (say which number in the note)

sections.title: Your calls from the business changes
sections.sub: These shape the rest, so they come first.

cards.title: Articles feed chapters. One set of conventions, or two?
cards.context: Today articles and letters follow their own conventions and the book follows the books'. Each difference is rework when an article becomes a chapter section.
rows: Article: digits always. Book: small counts in words, digits for measures and labels.
Article: a quoted line may stand on its own. Book: inline, except quick dialogue, a list of sample lines or the payoff line.
Article: a 600-word ballpark and a readability band. Book: no target.
Article: simple words. Book: richer, still plain.
options: b. Keep the article way for articles and letters
c. Mix (say which in the note)
cards.placeholder: Optional. Also say if your chimp-piece move (one line printed twice as a bridge) stays allowed

cards.title: Comparing a draft's words to your six March to May articles
cards.context: The writer lists every word your six true-voice pieces never use and watches the long abstract ones. The corpus is rebuilt from Notion each time.
options: b. Keep it for articles and letters

cards.title: The short-form track
cards.context: The 5x5x5 brainstorm, full storyboards for combos, the Content Rules doc. The skill it served (content-from-article) is gone, and the doc's log is empty.
options: b. Keep it for a future content card

cards.title: "Likes a 3-act structure for articles"
cards.context: A memory line. The rules now say headings never mark an act and each piece runs one arc.
options: b. Keep it, meaning a series told in 3 parts

cards.title: "David's case can be split into several people"
cards.context: A memory line from 7 Oct. Chapter 3 now tells David's arc once, then calls back.

cards.title: "Look in the brain first"
cards.context: Removed from the Book Rules on 4 Nov at your order and left as your call: whether that one sentence comes back as a rule.
options: b. Bring back that one sentence

sections.title: Rules I would cut or change
sections.sub: Each one either works against its own purpose, is beyond what the model can do well, or was made badly.

cards.title: Concrete nouns
rows: "Every noun is something the reader can see, touch or count."
Prefer concrete nouns. Explain ideas plainly.
Read literally in an argument chapter, it forces made-up images, the "vague metaphor no one uses" failure.

cards.title: "One honest limit per chapter"
rows: Calibrated confidence, with one honest limit per chapter (R22).
Drop the quota. Keep "a hedge only at a real limit".
A quota invites the disclaimer paragraph that was cut four times.

cards.title: Number targets
rows: Short sentences "1 in 7 to 1 in 5". A heading every 400 to 600 words. "At least one long winding sentence."
Keep each rule's job, drop the numbers. The script may still report them.
The model hits the number and misses the job.

cards.title: Exact parallel frames
rows: "Keep the frame exact" (R12), and paragraphs on one idea open the same way (R12a).
Parallel only when the items truly match, with the subject kept parallel. Drop R12a.
This push made taste test round 3 "robotic and repeated", and it fights "break a run" (R13).

cards.title: Carrying a case into other areas of life
rows: After every case, carry the idea into another area of life, then name a few more. A must (R16).
Polish, used when a case is narrow.
As a must it adds a stock "this works for X, Y and Z" paragraph after every case. It came from one article.

cards.title: Praised passages written as patterns
rows: The force paragraph, the "similarly:" analogy, the list of your structural moves and the ages series sit in the rules as moves to reach for.
Move them to the style bank as examples.
Loud examples get copied into every draft.

cards.title: Angry quotes inside rule text
rows: Your sharpest lines sit inside the rules they produced.
They move to the evidence beside the rule. The rule line stays calm.
The loudest quote makes the model over-apply that one rule.

cards.title: The banned-word list
rows: Circuit, variable, reasonable, eventually and 15 more, "always replaceable".
Drop the list. The concrete-noun rule does the job.
It came from one draft, and the model just swaps in synonyms.

cards.title: Claude scoring its own draft
rows: Before you see a chapter, Claude scores it on the six traits.
Drop it. The blind checkers replace it. Your scorecard stays.
It scored 7.5 the draft you nearly dropped.

cards.title: Your own story as warmth
rows: Warmth is your own short story, placed right after a case (R21).
Your stories come only from the brain, where one fits, never to fill a slot.
With no story for that spot, the model invents one or forces an "I, too".

cards.title: Protecting the author, reworded after your note
rows: Your worst moments clearly in the past. No line that reads against you out of context.

Being open and vulnerable is welcome, often good. Out: a line that reads against you out of context, such as a bad practice or a wealth flex. Your 5 Oct rule stays: a moment that shows you unfinished sits in the past, unless it pays off a vulnerable build.
said: looking bad and being emotionally available/vulnerable is a thin line often misrepresented by AI. the latter is OK even good to have in some cases.

cards.title: "Everyday" as one word
rows: One word only as an adjective ("an everyday habit"). As an adverb it is "every day". Your own typed words stay as typed.
The adverb form is a grammar mistake, and the rules say fix grammar.

cards.title: Clean-up
cards.context: Smaller changes that move or cut noise. None changes what a draft must do.
items: Worksheet rules: the verbatim-transcription rule moves to the mine skill, and "everything in build_worksheet.js is real" goes.
Rules for reading raw material (cut hedges, spot talking-out-loud) move to the mine skill.
"Call him X, and say so in the citation layer" goes. The cast in the brain and the anonymity note cover it.
Rules that point at a book line ("like Courage's narrator, CG 254") get their moves spelled out. Line references move to the evidence.
My unconfirmed readings inside rules come out until you confirm them.
The 8-line opening of the built-detail list becomes 3 lines.
Your quotes, the measurements, "[5 of 5]" tags and "(Added ... at his request)" lines move to the evidence beside each rule. The writer loads only the rule lines.
Notes about things that are not rules come out ("not a rule", "confirm with him if...").
Your recurring themes move to the brain. The extended-metaphor rules go, and "one image per beat" stays.
The too-heavy and too-light paragraphs and the named-things metric become one line: the numbers catch only gross failure.
Status notes inside rules ("the build doesn't handle figures yet") move to the handoff.
Old "open" and "proposed" labels in the Reel, Taste and Voice docs get cleaned when those cards are built.
The polish list loads only a few lines per card. The rest goes to the style bank.
options: Go, except the numbers in my note

sections.title: Clashes still open
sections.sub: Two rules say opposite things and nothing you decided settles them. No pick from me.

cards.title: Text you put in double quotes
rows: In a draft or comment, "" marks a sentence you strongly believe. Change at most a tenth (15 Oct).
An older memory line: a quoted explanation is a brief, rebuilt from scratch.
options: a. Both stand: "" in a draft or comment keeps 90%, a quoted explanation in chat is a brief
b. "" always keeps 90%. The older line goes

cards.title: "We"
rows: Your rules call "we" your bridge to the shared human beat, and chapter summaries use it.
The brand docs: "Voice: I. Never we or our team."
options: a. Only the business "we" (the company speaking) is banned. The shared human "we" stays everywhere
b. "We" is banned in brand copy only (bios, ads, pages). Articles and the book keep it

cards.title: Naming a pick when you choose
rows: rhyme-this ends with the option Claude would pick.
Your rule for grillings, and for this work: options with no pick.
options: a. No pick anywhere you choose
b. No pick in grillings and decisions. A pick allowed for rhyme options

sections.title: Already settled
sections.sub: Settled by your decisions or by newer rules. Go writes them this way.

cards.title: Settled items
items: Semicolons are banned everywhere (your 4 Nov call). Two memory lines that allow them get fixed.
Research follows R28 everywhere, articles included (your 4 Nov call). My reading: Insight 2 and the end note may still carry names, year and source.
Material comes from the brain only. References to the worksheet and the Testimony collection come out (27 Oct).
"Never condense" lines are retired for rule docs (your 4 Nov call). The Social, Reel, Taste and Content docs keep theirs until their cards are built.
The skill's "no checker agent" line goes, as in the plan you approved.
Letters lose the old "aim at about 320 words" line.
Money is fine with a struggle or a human side, never as a flex (4 Nov). The skill's old blanket ban goes.
Headings name an idea, never an act of the story (R31).
Chapters indent paragraphs. Key moments, articles, letters and case studies keep the gap (3 Nov).
The book may signpost. Articles never narrate their own structure (H5).
Fragments: none by default, and a deliberate one is flagged for you (H4).
Outside quotes: name and role in the prose, page and source in the end note (my reading).
The "planning agent only" memory line goes, since you want tasks done for you.
Insight 3: a question for a reader in your shoes, from an angle Insight 1 did not take.
One rules table in the brain, with copies written to the project and your Mac.
options: Go, except the numbers in my note
